problem: VLM-based socially compliant navigation relies on huge LLMs with high latency and energy cost, unsuitable for real-time robots. Existing RFT rewards (hard-match, character-level) are sparse or noisy for free-form social action text.
motivation: Robots in human-populated spaces need social compliance beyond collision avoidance, and must run on resource-constrained hardware. Small VLMs are efficient but have weak decision-making with scarce data, so RL-style post-training with a semantically meaningful reward may help.
key_idea: Combine a small sparse-MoE multimodal SLM with a three-stage SFT, RFT (GSPO), MoE fine-tuning pipeline, using a BERTScore-F1 semantic similarity reward (SSR) for RFT.
insight: Semantic-aware dense reward matters: SSR beats hard-level (SMS 0.551 vs 0.532) and character-level (0.510) rewards. GSPO+SSR beats GRPO+SSR and DPO. With scarce data, 4 experts with top-1 routing works best, a frozen SigLIP encoder is preferable, and multi-turn training/inference helps. The small model outperforms GPT-4o and Claude at a fraction of the size, though the evaluation is small (60 test images) and text-similarity based.
method: Stage 1 SFT: image-text alignment (captioning loss, initialized from LLaVA-1.5-58K), then SFT on SNEI multi-turn conversations mapping images to actions (direction/speed).
Stage 2 RFT: GSPO (sequence-level importance ratio, group size 8, KL regularization) optimizes the SLM with group-normalized advantages.
Semantic Similarity Reward (SSR): reward = BERTScore-F1 between generated action text and ground truth, giving dense semantic feedback vs. exact/character matching.
Stage 3 MoE fine-tuning: alternating FFN design (half of layers are sparse MoE) with softmax router and top-k routing (best 4 experts, k=1), multi-turn conversational fine-tuning.
Backbone choices: frozen SigLIP vision encoder + Phi-2-2.7B SLM; data augmentation (non-geometric lighting/weather) doubles training set to 530 images.

setting.backbone: Phi-2-2.7B MoE SLM + SigLIP (frozen vision encoder), fine-tuned
setting.training_data: LLaVA-1.5-58K initialization, then SNEI augmented training set (530 images from 265 originals); SFT then RFT then MoEFT
setting.observation: single monocular RGB image with scene/prompt text (multi-turn conversation)
setting.action_space: high-level text action commands (direction such as forward/slight turn/stop, plus speed level)

numbers.eval_set_note: 60 test images of SNEI (325 images, 265 train)
numbers.extra: trained on augmented data (530 images); 5.74B params, FPS 1.709; metrics are semantic similarity, not SR
numbers.evidence: Table 2 accuracy comparisons, Augmented dataset row; Table 1 efficiency

numbers.extra: trained on original 265 images without augmentation

numbers_note: No standard navigation metrics (SR/SPL); only text-similarity metrics on the SNEI test set. Baselines GPT-4o SMS 0.376 and Claude 0.417 are not included.
results: SocialNav-MoE (5.74B params, 1.709 FPS) reaches SMS 0.551, 46.5% and 32.1% above GPT-4o (0.376) and Claude (0.417), using about 3% of their parameters and 8.1x/19.6x higher FPS. GSPO+SSR beats DPO (SMS 0.527) and GRPO+SSR (0.531).
limitations: Tiny dataset (60 test images) and evaluation via text-similarity metrics rather than closed-loop navigation; no real-robot or simulator tests.
Social norms are ambiguous, so GT may not be uniquely correct (failure analysis shows acceptable alternative actions).
Comparison with GPT-4o/Claude is zero-shot with approximate parameter counts, so it is not a like-for-like comparison.
